## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

Done and verified. Here's what I found and changed.

## The defect is real, and I proved it end-to-end

Everything in the handoff checked out against `origin/main`. The one item marked NOT verified — that un-OPF'd bytes actually reach a remote — is now verified. A RED test against unmodified code showed `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs`, with OPF enabled, pushing both checkpoint refs to a bare remote with **zero** OPF invocations and no `Entire-OPF-Applied` trailer on the commits that landed. A second test showed a deliberately failing OPF runtime didn't stop the push either.

## The fix

`runOPFForCheckpointRefs` (bool) became `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` (error) at `manual_commit_push.go:249`. It resolves the decision and runs the rewrite; reporting moves to the caller, because the two callers need opposite failure surfaces:

- `prePushCheckpointRefs:407` — warns and returns nil, unchanged. A checkpoint failure must never block the user's own `git push`.
- `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs:455` — returns an error with the refs left queued, matching the checkpoint-policy branch three lines above it.

Both `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` call sites are now behind the gate; I confirmed there are only two, and that the v1 path's rewrite has only its one guarded call site.

## On the caveat you flagged

I checked `doctor_migrate.go:100-115` rather than assuming. The error is wrapped with `%w`, so its `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` → `NewSilentError` branch still matches; otherwise it wraps as `push migrated refs: …`, exits non-zero, and the refs stay queued for the next `git push`, which applies OPF. Nothing breaks.

**One behaviour change worth putting in the PR description:** `doctor migrate` only reaches this code when a TTY is present, so answering yes to "Push N migrated checkpoint ref(s) now?" with OPF enabled now shows a second prompt — the standard "Run OpenAI Privacy Filter on these checkpoints?" — unless `prompt_default` or `ENTIRE_OPF` already decides it. That second prompt is the point: it's the decision that was previously hard-coded to skip.

## Verification

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean (0 issues), and full `mise run test:ci` passes — unit, integration, and the Vogon canary E2E (4/4). The four pre-existing `TestPushQueuedCheckpointRefs*` tests still pass alongside the two new ones.

it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and

commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Four reviewers, deduped and applied. `mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean, full `test:ci` green, and I re-confirmed both tests still fail with the gate removed — the rework didn't hollow them out.

## Fixed

**Production** — `manual_commit_push.go` is now *smaller* than before this cleanup:
- `redact.OPFEnabled()` moved inside `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` as an early return. Both call sites collapse from a nested double-`if` to one line, and a future third caller can no longer half-apply the gate by remembering the function but forgetting the flag. Simplification and altitude reviewers both pointed here.
- Cut the 6-line call-site comment in `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs` — every clause was already in the gate's doc, the function's doc, or the error string on the next line.
- Cut the sentence narrating the change's history rather than the code.

**Tests** — net smaller and materially stronger:
- Both tests moved onto the existing `setupGitRefsOPFRepo` fixture, which writes sentinel-bearing sessions through the real backend. The success test now asserts the sentinel is actually **scrubbed** and that the *rewritten* object is what reached the remote — not merely that a trailer is present. That's a better test than the one I wrote.
- Deleted my hand-rolled `remoteCommitMessage` (`testutil.RunGit` already did it, and the hash round-trip was unnecessary).
- Extracted `assertRefsAbsentFromRemote` and pointed the pre-existing `PolicyBlocked` test at it too, removing a third copy of that block.
- Dropped the `batchCallCount` assertion — already pinned by a sibling test.

## Skipped, with reasons

- **Gate moved inside `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` with a failure-policy enum** (altitude's main recommendation). Structurally better, but I checked `CleanupPushedShadowBranches` and it deletes on session-state protection alone, independent of whether the push landed — so running it on the withhold path, as that restructure would, is a behaviour change I won't make under a cleanup remit.
- **Empty-queue prompt.** Genuinely the sharpest finding: the gate resolves the OPF decision before anything knows the queue is non-empty, so `doctor migrate` can ask "Run OPF? Adds ~30s", get a yes, then print "No queued refs to push". Rare (the command just migrated the refs), pre-existing on the pre-push side, and fixing it changes when a prompt appears — so it's a note for the PR, not a silent change.
- **Queue + ref lookups running twice per flush** — pre-existing; the fix threads state through a shared function well outside this diff. Worth putting in the PR: on reftable repos each `repo.Reference` spawns git subprocesses, so a 200-ref migration backfill pays ~800 avoidable spawns.
- **Egress assertion in `push_common.go`** covering both backends — needs per-process decision plumbing; the reviewer itself scoped it as a follow-up.
- **Guard test** — the reviewer argued against one, and I agree: the required-parameter version would be strictly stronger, and a grep-guard weaker than what the type system already gives here.

Still uncommitted, same two files.
